speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the nature of your chest pain and how it relates to your vomiting? I also need to know how long these symptoms have been present.

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your inability to communicate and the classic presentation of forceful vomiting followed by severe chest pain, I need to act immediately to confirm a suspected esophageal rupture. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray. REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_with_contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest X-ray: Free mediastinal air visible, suggesting perforation. CT Chest with contrast: Data not available in current records.

speaker: Doctor
text: The chest X-ray showing free mediastinal air confirms a perforation, likely Boerhaave syndrome given the history of forceful vomiting. DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave syndrome (spontaneous esophageal rupture).
